title: A Flesh-Eating Fly Is Back. The Fix: 100 Million More Flies a Week

scenes.text: To kill this fly, America breeds a hundred million of them a week.
The New World screwworm. Its maggots don't eat dead meat. They burrow into living cattle, deer, even dogs.
A female lays up to 300 eggs at a time, 3,000 in her life. Untreated, a wound can kill an animal in about a week.
But she has one weakness. She mates only once. So scientists sterilize males with radiation and drop them from planes.
Wild females mate with a sterile male, lay eggs that never hatch, and the population crashes. That's how the US wiped it out in 1966.
Now it's back: tens of thousands of cases in Mexico, the first US cases in 2026. The cure for the fly is a hundred million more flies.

description:
The New World screwworm fly lays its eggs in living animals, and its larvae feed on living flesh. The United States eradicated it in 1966 with the sterile insect technique: females mate only once, so releasing radiation-sterilized males by the millions makes the next generation never hatch.
The fly is now back: Mexico has recorded tens of thousands of cases since late 2024 and the first US animal cases were confirmed in 2026. A USDA facility in Panama produces about 100 million sterile flies a week, with new plants under construction in Mexico and Texas.
Would you have believed the answer to a plague of flies is more flies?
subject: screwworm fly
first_comment: The first trial of the sterile fly method, on the island of Curacao in the 1950s, wiped the screwworm out in seven weeks. What other pest would you fight this way?
